method: Two-fresh-coordinate fixed-bias embedding combined with disjoint tensor powers and exact U/I/G identities.
bounded_objective: Determine whether universal GU(a,b) can be reduced, with the same constants, to one fixed output-bias slice while allowing a uniform sublinear terminal.
prior_status: Universal GU was reduced to a signed-residual estimate on balanced functions; no direct fixed-bias GU equivalence was established.
mathematical_delta: Proved universal GU(a,b) equivalent to GU(a,b)+o(N) on the single slice E F=1/2. Every arbitrary-bias seed embeds with bounded overhead erased by tensor powers. No admissible pair was proved.

verification.arithmetic_scope: Exact rational Walsh masses and binary64 logarithms; the all-dimensional reduction is analytic.

retained_hypotheses: The fixed-slice estimate must be uniform over every Boolean function with E F=1/2.
The additive terminal must be o(N) uniformly over that slice.
Two fresh coordinates and disjoint tensor copies are used in the hardness embedding.
next_action: Use p_empty=1/4 on the fixed-bias slice to seek a uniform sublinear bound on the aggregate mismatch, testing embedded tensor powers of the activation witness and shared-coordinate counterfamily.
blockers: No admissible pair a,b has been proved on the fixed-bias slice.
The slice is not restriction-closed, so the reduction requires the tensor embedding rather than direct slice induction.
